verdict: Trustworthy and complete enough to hand to the team after a short patch pass. Every sampled Priority card carries the reference-side corrections faithfully: refuted mechanisms are removed or relabelled (Buzz 15 render classes, QM character offsets, the disabled Grok Bot rate limiter, Teams keywords not counted as triggers, the Grok Bot sandbox enforcement mechanism marked unknown, Buzz roster validation done on the client), corrected prevalence counts are used, and the Verevon-side text follows verification.verevon closely, including approachAdjustment and the architecture constraints. Examples: thread:append reused instead of a new space:post decision; Session Core, not the Application Plane, as the first event emitter; a notification-core consumer instead of a wider gateway allowlist; Quarry as the SSRF boundary. Every cited code location I opened in CoresSystem at afb83928 supports its sentence, and specific reference figures I traced back (500 ms debounce, 4096-character rule cap, 2.2 s headline rotation, 4 s SSE open timeout, 9-participant DM cap, 5 MB broker cap) exist in the inputs or the reference source. The four Recommended-to-Nice-to-have demotions and the F-t1-005 demotion read consistently. The problems found are local. One Priority sentence says search is permission-aware in 4 of 5 references, although per-hit re-authorization is verified only in Buzz. One Priority card says the agent self-API is low cost although verification raised its effort. Three cards give three different lists of gateway search routes. There are a few wrong or overclaiming provenance tags, two 'ships' and 'every' overstatements, one citation that points at the wrong code, and stale plane text in Appendix B. None of these changes a tier or a recommendation.
